title: Employer Benefit Charging Credit and Reimbursement Billing Terms
content:
Employer Benefit Charging classes differ in how an employer pays for its charges and where a credit against those charges appears. Whether a credit arises for a recovered overpayment, a cancelled payment or an appeal reversal is set the same way in all seven classes.

| Charge class | Pays its charges dollar for dollar by reimbursement bill instead of through its rate | Recovered overpayment principal credited back | Cancelled payment's charge credited back | Charges credited back when an appeal decision relieves the employer | Where a credit appears |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Separating Employer — Most Recent | No | Yes | Yes | Yes | Next quarter's statement |
| Base Period Employer — Proportional Share | No | Yes | Yes | Yes | Next quarter's statement |
| Continuing Part-Time Base Period Employer | No | Yes | Yes | Yes | Next quarter's statement |
| Combined Wage Claim Contributing Employer | No | Yes | Yes | Yes | Next quarter's statement |
| Extended Benefits State-Share Employer | No | Yes | Yes | Yes | Next quarter's statement |
| Reimbursing Nonprofit Employer — Dollar-for-Dollar | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Next quarter's reimbursement bill |
| Reimbursing Governmental Employer — Dollar-for-Dollar | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Next quarter's reimbursement bill |

## Basis Q&A

**Which classes are billed for their charges?** Reimbursing Nonprofit Employer — Dollar-for-Dollar and Reimbursing Governmental Employer — Dollar-for-Dollar. The five contributory classes pay through their rate.

**Where does a reimbursing employer see a credit?** On its next quarter's reimbursement bill. A contributory employer sees a credit on its next quarter's statement.

**Is a cancelled payment's charge credited back for an Extended Benefits State-Share Employer?** Yes; the cancelled-payment credit is available in every class.
